description: What counts as landing on a pad. Every number follows from the pad (configs/targets/objects.json), the vehicle (configs/robot_quadrotor_fastphysics.jsonc) or a measurement in the simulator (docs/aerovla_oft_gen_v3.md, 'Landing in the simulator'); none is tuned to a result.

vehicle.half_span_from: rotor hubs at +-0.253 m on both axes plus the propeller radius
vehicle.rest_offset_from: height of the body origin above the surface it rests on, measured at spawn (0.193 m) and on a pad's marking (0.158 m)

touchdown.definition: the collision topic names the pad or its marking while the vehicle is above the pad's top surface; the simulator holds the vehicle still from that moment
touchdown.landing_region_from: pad half-width (7.0 m) minus the vehicle half-span (0.4 m): the whole vehicle stands on the pad
touchdown.max_vertical_speed_from: the action range allows 1.0 m/s of descent and the teacher's final descent is 0.5 m/s; half-way between the two separates a controlled descent from one at full rate
touchdown.max_horizontal_speed_from: a quarter of the 2.0 m/s the action range allows forward

stages.aligned_from: a quarter of the pad's width: the marking's centre lies inside the middle of the down view from every flight height used

teacher.align_radius_from: an eighth of the pad's width
teacher.commit_from: once the vehicle is low over the pad and still within a quarter of its width of the centre it keeps descending; without this a drift of a few decimetres past the align radius turned the label into 'turn back' just above the surface (pilot flight pilot-9000)

evaluator.description: How a stable physical landing is read from a flight's log, from Gen-v3c on (docs/gen_v3c_hard_negative_grounding.md). The first reading asked for a reported vertical speed of at most 0.05 m/s at each decision; in two of 24 landings of the canonical validation run the simulator kept reporting 0.04-0.095 m/s for a vehicle whose position did not change by a millimetre, and both were counted as not stable. This reading uses positions only: the contact on a pad from above (touchdown), the last `stable_position_window_steps` decisions all at the contact's height, and no more movement between them than the two displacement limits. Which pad it is, the landing region and the speed of the contact are judged separately, as before. Fixed before any flight was judged with it; earlier runs keep the reading they were recorded with.
evaluator.from: measured over windows of three decisions in 63 teacher landings and 24 landings of the model (canonical validation and test starts, 194 windows of a standing vehicle): standing, at most 0.0000 m horizontally and 0.0003 m vertically; a window that still holds the last decision of the descent, up to 0.20 m vertically; the final descent, at least 0.45 m vertically. 0.05 m is more than a hundred times the first and a ninth of the last, and is what the finalizer's own limit (0.1 m/s) allows in one decision. A vehicle hovering at an approach stop moved 0.001-0.05 m vertically and 0.2-1.4 m horizontally in such a window, so stillness alone does not tell a hover from a landing; the contact and the height do.

finalizer.description: Low-level end of a landing (src/visual_search/finalizer.py), active only when the sentence asks for a landing. It latches LANDED after a contact made while descending has stayed still for `stable_decisions` decisions, then passes no motion command on and disarms. It reads the contact report and the vehicle's own positions; it is not told what the vehicle stands on. Fixed before any flight was judged with it.
finalizer.descent_from: a commanded descent larger than the policy's own stop band on the down axis (8 % of its 1.0 m range)
finalizer.speed_from: measured over one decision from the vehicle's positions. In 61 recorded teacher landings the vehicle moved at most 0.029 m/s vertically and 0.0 m/s horizontally while standing on a pad, and descended at a median of 0.51 m/s; 0.1 m/s is three times the first and a fifth of the second
finalizer.stable_from: three decisions in a row, one second between the first and the last
